- The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, cited by 2025-edition entry numbers (LLM01:2025 to LLM09:2025): all entry Descriptions except ASI07 reference these; Appendix A supplies mappings for all ten ASI entries [BT] (pp. 6, 9–40).
- OWASP AIVSS: scoring and prioritization; Core Risks mapped per entry [BT] (pp. 6, 12, 15, 24, 36, 39–41).
- OWASP CycloneDX and the AIBOM OWASP Project: component inventory and provenance, which the Top 10 says it builds on [BT] (p. 41).
- The OWASP Non-Human Identities Top 10 (2025): mapped in Appendix C [BT] (pp. 6, 42–43).
- The GenAI Security project's CTI initiative and its incident response guide [BT] (p. 44).
- The OWASP GenAI Red Teaming Guide: named only in the licence page's attribution guideline [BT] (p. 1).
- Agentic identity platforms named as examples: Microsoft Entra, AWS Bedrock Agents, Salesforce Agentforce, Workday's Agentic System of Record (ASOR), Google Vertex AI [BT] (ASI03, p. 17); mcp-run-python named as a framework sandbox [BT] (ASI05, p. 23).
- Each entry's References list (titles and URLs as printed in the entry sections above), and the security researchers and firms named as links in Appendix D [BT] (pp. 11–49).

## Positions the author explicitly frames against

- *Unnecessary autonomy.* Deploying agentic behaviour where it is not needed expands the attack surface without adding value; the advice is to avoid it (Least-Agency) (p. 7).
- *Overlapping guidance.* The Top 10 aims to simplify and connect existing guidance, not add to an overload of it (p. 6).
- *Perimeter-based security for multi-agent systems.* Decentralised architecture, varying autonomy and uneven trust make it ineffective (ASI07, p. 27).
- *Ad-hoc conventions and syntax-only checks for tools.* Tool permissions go in policy stanzas rather than ad-hoc conventions, and tool calls are validated for intended semantics rather than syntax alone (ASI02, pp. 13–14).
- *Model-generated rationales as the user's risk summary.* A plain-language risk summary is to be provided instead (ASI09, p. 35).
- *Attempting full semantic alignment across agents.* Typed contracts help with structure, but semantic divergence across agents remains inherent, so mitigations focus on integrity, provenance and controlled communication (ASI07, p. 29).
- *eval, root and direct agent-to-production paths.* Ban eval in production agents, never run as root, prevent direct agent-to-production systems (ASI05, p. 22).
- *Open registration and agent-held keys.* No open registration for inter-agent security (ASI04, p. 20); keys must never be directly available to agents (ASI10, p. 38).

## Citation and source-integrity notes

**Conversion.** The original is a 57-page PDF exported from Word (title field "Microsoft Word - OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 12.6.docx", created 2025-12-10 13:11 NZDT, letter size), held at `sources/original/owasp-agentic-top10-2026.pdf` (sha256 a2db94cd00b08e0b3a5e5b619afe024bdbcd74503111085705e4f3dd886fcb5c), with a born-digital text layer. The tape `sources/converted/owasp-agentic-top10-2026.md` (2,172 lines, 13,820 words) is that layer extracted with `pdftotext -layout` (poppler 26.08.0). Post-conversion check: 57 form feeds for 57 pages; footers run "Page 1" to "Page 56" with p. 55 absent; the end (Project Supporters, p. 56) is present; no truncation marker. About 250 words a text page; four pages are table of contents and one is a logo grid.

**Page anchors.** Printed p. N is PDF p. N+1. In the tape, p. 1 begins at line 11, p. 6 at 182, p. 8 at 252, p. 9 (ASI01) at 298, p. 12 (ASI02) at 404, p. 15 (ASI03) at 527, p. 18 (ASI04) at 654, p. 21 (ASI05) at 772, p. 24 (ASI06) at 873, p. 27 (ASI07) at 996, p. 30 (ASI08) at 1118, p. 33 (ASI09) at 1245, p. 36 (ASI10) at 1372, p. 39 (Appendix A) at 1476, p. 41 at 1566, p. 42 at 1590, p. 44 (Appendix D) at 1681, p. 50 at 1960, p. 52 at 2028, and p. 56 at 2132. Each page's footer closes it.

**What came from renders, not the tape.** Three pages were rendered at 110 dpi. On p. 13 the text layer garbles the title of ASI02 scenario 4 into symbols (tape line 456); the render reads "Internal Query → External Exfiltration". Printed p. 55 (PDF p. 56) has no text layer at all (two consecutive form feeds at tape line 2132); its sponsor statement and logos were read from the render, so nothing from it carries `[V]`. The positions of the ASI badges in the p. 8 diagram were read from the render; its labels are also in the tape (lines 252–292).
